title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant I

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant I (theme family: environment and nature). PART 1.1 - level A1-A2 - scored items 1, 2 and 3 (0-5 for the three together). Three short personal questions, asked one after another. The candidate has 30 seconds to answer each question. There is NO preparation time. The examiner reads the opening words and then the three questions exactly as printed; after each question the examiner gives the sound signal (chime) and times 30 seconds.

questions.q:
CEFR MULTILEVEL MOCK - SPEAKING - VARIANT I - PART 1.1 (A1-A2, items 1-3, 30 seconds per answer, no preparation)

EXAMINER OPENING (read aloud, word for word):
'Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime).'

[STAGE DIRECTION: give the chime before each answer. Time 30 seconds. Say 'Thank you.' when the time is up, then move straight on to the next question. Do not help the candidate and do not repeat a question more than once.]

QUESTION 1 (item 1) - 30 seconds
'Are there any trees, flowers or plants near your home? Tell me about them.'

[chime - 30 seconds - 'Thank you.']

QUESTION 2 (item 2) - 30 seconds
'What is the weather usually like in your town in spring?'

[chime - 30 seconds - 'Thank you.']

QUESTION 3 (item 3) - 30 seconds
'Which season of the year do you like best? Tell me why.'

[chime - 30 seconds - 'Thank you.']

EXAMINER CLOSING FOR THIS PART: 'Thank you. Now we will look at some photographs.'

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant I (theme family: environment and nature). PART 1.2 - level B1 - scored items 4, 5 and 6 (0-5 for the three together). Two photographs on one theme are shown to the candidate. Question 4 (compare and describe the two pictures) = 45 seconds. Questions 5 and 6 (personal opinion, justified) = 30 seconds each. The questions are asked one after another. There is NO preparation time. The system holds no image files: the examiner either displays two photographs matching the bracketed descriptions or reads the descriptions aloud slowly before asking question 4.

questions.q:
CEFR MULTILEVEL MOCK - SPEAKING - VARIANT I - PART 1.2 (B1, items 4-6, no preparation)

[PICTURE 1: a narrow apartment balcony in a block of flats, completely filled with home-grown food - tomato plants tied to canes in white buckets, spring onions and herbs in old tin cans along the railing, a small watering can on the floor, a woman in her sixties checking the leaves; behind the railing, rooftops, satellite dishes and other apartment blocks in the afternoon sun.]

[PICTURE 2: a very large open vegetable field in the countryside, seen from the edge of the road - long, perfectly straight rows of green crops running to the horizon, a tractor with a wide spraying boom moving across the middle distance leaving a fine mist behind it, no people anywhere near the camera, a flat grey sky and a line of pylons along the far edge of the field.]

EXAMINER (read aloud, word for word):
'Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?'

[STAGE DIRECTION: show or describe both photographs, then give the chime. Question 4 is timed at 45 seconds; questions 5 and 6 at 30 seconds each.]

QUESTION 4 (item 4) - 45 seconds - compare and describe
'What do you see in these pictures? Compare the two places and say how food is being grown in each of them.'

[chime - 45 seconds - 'Thank you.']

QUESTION 5 (item 5) - 30 seconds - opinion, justified
'Would you like to grow some of your own food at home? Why, or why not?'

[chime - 30 seconds - 'Thank you.']

QUESTION 6 (item 6) - 30 seconds - opinion, justified
'Some people say that food grown close to a city is better for the environment than food brought from far away. What do you think?'

[chime - 30 seconds - 'Thank you.']

EXAMINER CLOSING FOR THIS PART: 'Thank you. That is the end of part one.'

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant I (theme family: environment and nature). PART 2 - level B2 - scored item 7 (0-5). One picture and three questions are presented AT ONCE. The candidate has 1 MINUTE to think and then 2 MINUTES to answer all three questions together. The candidate is NOT required to describe the picture - it is there only to bring the theme to mind. Give paper and a pencil for notes during the preparation minute. The system holds no image files: the examiner either displays a photograph matching the bracketed description or reads the description aloud.

questions.q:
CEFR MULTILEVEL MOCK - SPEAKING - VARIANT I - PART 2 (B2, item 7, 1 minute preparation, 2 minutes speaking)

EXAMINER OPENING (read aloud, word for word):
'Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph.'

[PICTURE: the corner of an ordinary family kitchen with three separate waste containers standing side by side under the worktop - one half full of flattened cardboard and newspaper, one holding glass jars and bottles, one with food peelings; a young man at the sink is rinsing an empty jam jar under the tap before putting it in, and a cloth shopping bag hangs on the door handle behind him.]

[STAGE DIRECTION: say clearly - 'You do not have to describe the picture.' Then read all three questions aloud once, unhurried, and leave them in front of the candidate. Start the preparation minute. After one minute give the chime and time two minutes for the whole answer. Do not interrupt; at two minutes say 'Thank you.']

THE THREE QUESTIONS (asked together, answered together within the two minutes):
1. 'Tell me about something you have done at home, at school or at work to produce less waste.'
2. 'How has doing that changed your daily routine, and how did the people around you react?'
3. 'In general, what do you think most influences whether ordinary people change their everyday habits to protect the environment - money, laws, information, or the example of other people?'

[1 minute preparation - chime - 2 minutes for all three questions - 'Thank you. That is the end of part two.']

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant I (theme family: environment and nature). PART 3 - level C1 - scored item 8 (0-6). One topic statement is shown with two lists beside it, FOR and AGAINST, three points in each. The candidate chooses TWO points from EACH list and gives a balanced argument representing both sides. 1 MINUTE preparation with paper and pencil, then 2 MINUTES of continuous speech. EXAMINER NOTE - OFFICIAL SCORING: items 1-3 (Part 1.1) together = 0-5; items 4-6 (Part 1.2) together = 0-5; item 7 (Part 2) = 0-5; item 8 (Part 3) = 0-6; maximum raw score 21. questions.q:
CEFR MULTILEVEL MOCK - SPEAKING - VARIANT I - PART 3 (C1, item 8, 1 minute preparation, 2 minutes speaking)

EXAMINER OPENING (read aloud, word for word):
'Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime).'

TOPIC STATEMENT (show to the candidate, and read aloud once):
'Entry to national parks and other protected natural areas should be strictly limited to a small number of visitors each day.'

FOR
1. Crowds wear away paths, disturb wildlife and leave more litter than the land can absorb.
2. Money from a limited number of permits can pay for rangers, repairs and long-term conservation.
3. A quiet park gives visitors the experience they actually came for, instead of queues and full car parks.

AGAINST
1. Wild places belong to everyone, and a daily limit favours those who can book early or pay more.
2. Guesthouses, guides, cafes and transport in nearby towns depend on a steady flow of visitors.
3. People who are never allowed into nature are less likely to care about protecting it.

[STAGE DIRECTION: leave the statement and both lists in front of the candidate for the whole task. Remind them once: 'Choose two points from the FOR list and two points from the AGAINST list.' Start the preparation minute and give paper and a pencil. After one minute give the chime and time two minutes. Do not interrupt or prompt; at two minutes say 'Thank you. That is the end of the test.']

[1 minute preparation - chime - 2 minutes speaking]
